transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Trump also announced a new program to give farmers one-time payments for diesel fuel costs. This program is worth $8 billion.
NPR has learned that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth paid a secret visit to Israel yesterday. He met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
And Pierre's Daniel Estrin has more from Tel Aviv.
There's been no official comment by the U.S. or Israel, but a person familiar with the matter speaking on condition of anonymity said Hegseth met with Netanyahu in Israel.
President Trump and Netanyahu have been speaking publicly, suggesting the possibility of a new strike on Iran.
Netanyahu's staff released a video of him next to fighter jets, where he appears to be speaking on the phone with Trump.
Donald, we have a job to finish. You said it, and we'll finish it together.
Israel's military announced it's on the highest state of alert ahead of Israel's elections next week on Tuesday. Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Trump administration is banning the Chinese AI model DeepSeek from the IT systems of federal civilian agencies.
As NPR's John Brewich reports, the Department of Homeland Security cites data security risks.
DeepSeek is one of China's leading AI models, and it sparked concern in the U.S. last year when it demonstrated capabilities that many here didn't think Chinese AI labs could pull off.
The Department of Homeland Security is now ordering civilian government agencies not to use DeepSeek AI and to ban it, as well as other software developed using DeepSeek from IT systems.
It says DeepSeek's models present, quote, "multiple threat vectors" and flags the risk that China could get actionable intelligence on the U.S. through DeepSeek or spread malware.
The move is the latest in a series of steps by both sides to regulate or restrict the other's AI. John Brewich, NPR News.
People in the Canadian province of Alberta have voted to reject separation from Canada.
And Karbenchuk reports this brings to an end a long campaign.
The latest results show 76 percent of Albertans want to remain in Canada, about 24 percent voted to begin the process of separation.
Prime Minister Mark Carney says the vote sends a message that Albertans made a clear choice for unity and to build together.
Premier Doug Ford of Ontario says now it's up to the rest of the country to deliver on commitments to Alberta by building new pipelines and unlocking the Western province's abundant oil and gas resources.
Pro-separatist groups say they're taking a wait-and-see attitude, and the leader of the Let Alberta Decide campaign, Keith Wilson, says there will likely be future talks about the province's role in Canada.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenchuk in Toronto.
This is NPR.
French officials imposed curfews overnight in parts of several cities, including Paris.
It's to stop unrest and some rioting that broke out last weekend.
Italy is deploying troops after riots in Milan.
There has been similar unrest in Albania, Portugal and Spain.
Authorities in Australia have charged a man with intentionally attacking a female lawmaker.
The suspect, Brendan Nugent, is accused of intentionally driving into lawmaker Helen Haynes.
She is hospitalized in critical condition.
In the U.S., another nor'easter is headed for the East Coast. Forecasters say strong winds and coastal flooding are expected from the Carolinas to New England.
The Tampa Bay Rays will face the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series.
From member station W.M.N.F., Sean Kinon reports Tampa clinched a berth in the fall classic last night with a win at home.
The Rays won the American League Championship in six games, with a 7-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians in St. Petersburg.
It was the Rays' third win in as many days after a rainout in Cleveland.
The World Series begins Friday in Milwaukee, where the National League Champion Brewers will host the first two games.
The series then shifts to Tropicana Field in St. Pete for games 3, 4 and, if necessary, game 5.
This will be the Rays' third World Series appearance. Neither the Brewers nor the Rays have ever won the World Series,
and both teams rank in the lower half of team payrolls in Major League Baseball.
For NPR News, I'm Sean Kinon in Tampa.
ora.com/npr to learn more.
